Few Geniuses never experience Delusions of Grandeur, Fewer yet call them delusions

The Godhead class should never have existed. An Idle speculation, an upper bound curiosity, a concoction of an Ill mind to fell a fleet with a single ship, yet here it stands. Easily dwarfing a star citadel the Godhead is a prototype Super capital unsanctioned to be built by even the company who conceived it. Every metric of the ship is beyond excessive, it would be unfeasible both logistically and physically to operate if not for the numerous experimental systems and augmentations that adorn the vessel.

A glass cannon taken to its logical extreme,

The hull of the mirage class is little more than a scaffold for weapon mounts, wrapped around overclocked engines, a temperamental phase drive, and reactors straining to barely meet the energy demands. These concessions place the mirage into a doctrinal rock and hard place. The fragile nature of the mirage and it's exorbitant cost often relegate it to a back line escort in spite of all design decisions pointing to a purpose of harrasment and gurrellia warfare. 

Rumors persist of pilots wielding the Mirage to devastating effect.

Where the Flood sustains a fleets, its sister frame, the Drought consumes them. 

The shared frame is the extent of the resemblance; virtually every internal system has been stripped and rebuilt around salvage arms, construction rails, and the hangar infrastructure needed to deploy mining, salvage, and prospecting equipment at scale. The result is more akin to a mobile shipyard, capable of servicing, constructing, and breaking down vessels comparable in size to domain era hulks.

Whether this is considered impressive or deeply unsettling tends to depend on which side of the operation one is on.

The Flood-class was Diable Avionics' answer to a question most engineers and logisticians had stopped asking, whether a single hull could sustain an entire operation's logistical needs. The answer was yes, provided the caveat of concentrating that much strategic value in a single hull. The Flood is specifically characterized by a minimalist modular frame that can be easily outfitted with vast logistical solutions, earning the Flood a coveted position within the fleets with the needs to demand one. It's armament, while not trivial, exists to deter small scale privateers and is ultimately overwhelmed by most vessels above a destroyer class.

This variant's hull is dominated by an array of super-industrial anti-matter containment spheres, maintained by a dedicated crew of high-stress technicians. Due to the immense capacity of the Flood, few fuel depots can actually fill the vessel to capacity. Nevertheless, seasoned fleet commanders are diligent to enforce a strict exclusion zone around it, as even when under-filled, a small incident can prove catastrophic.
